      <title>Isaias strengthens to become first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 season</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/09/isaias-strengthens-first-atlantic-hurricane-2026</link>
      <description><p>Storm expected to make landfall on US’s northern Gulf coast with risk of flash floods and isolated river flooding</p><p>Isaias has become the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with wind speeds of 80mph and a minimum pressure of 975mb. It is expected to strengthen to a category 2 hurricane as it approaches the US’s northern Gulf coast on Friday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).</p><p>As a result of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/sep/26/what-is-el-nino-causes-can-we-reduce-risks">the strong El Niño</a>, it has been a notably quiet Atlantic hurricane season. The first hurricane of the season has not formed this late since 8 October 1905, which pre-dates the satellite era (1960s) for tracking hurricanes that has allowed for more non-landfall hurricanes to be discovered.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/09/isaias-strengthens-first-atlantic-hurricane-2026">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Latin American organised crime ‘may operate in 16 European countries’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/13/latin-america-organised-crime-cartels-drugs-cocaine-europe</link>
      <description><p>Cocaine seizures in Europe are up more than fivefold in 10 years as a host of cartels take root. A four-month Guardian investigation reveals the true scale of a continent-wide shift</p><p>A four-month investigation by the Guardian has revealed that the surge in cocaine trafficking to Europe is directly linked to the expanding presence of Latin American criminal networks in Europe, where they have forged close ties with local mafia organisations.</p><p>The investigation, utilising databases, police and intelligence agencies, along with interviews with judges, prosecutors and experts from eight countries, shows that cartels and factions from Colombia, Brazil, Ecuador, Venezuela, Mexico and the US are active in at least 12 European countries. Between 2014 and 2024, there was a <a href="https://www.euda.europa.eu/publications/european-drug-report/2026/drug-supply-production-and-precursors_en">471% rise in the quantity of cocaine seized</a> and more local laboratories processing cocaine derivatives were dismantled.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/13/latin-america-organised-crime-cartels-drugs-cocaine-europe">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>In today’s newsletter: The prime minister is calling for closer ties with the EU, but what could this actually amount to?</p><p>Good morning. Conservative governments long insisted there was no evidence of Russian interference in the Brexit vote. He was 34.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/13/tuesday-briefing-could-burnham-take-britain-back-towards-the-eu">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Andy Burnham will take Britain back into European Union, Neil Kinnock claims – UK politics live</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/oct/13/andy-burnham-brexit-eu-europe-neil-kinnock-lobby-wes-streeting-labour-prisoner-early-release-uk-politics-latest-news-updates</link>
      <description><p>Former Labour leader says he believes the prime minister has an ‘authentic commitment’ to taking the UK back into the EU</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/oct/12/andy-burnham-britain-eu-brexit-reset">Andy Burnham promises ‘serious dialogue’ over UK’s relationship with EU</a></p></li></ul><p>Good morning. In his long statement to MPs yesterday, <strong>Andy Burnham</strong> was evasive when asked whether he wanted his planned renegotiation of Britain’s relationship with the EU to result in a Labour-led government, after the next election, rejoining. In response to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/oct/12/uk-politics-live-tories-andy-burnham-russian-interference-brexit-eu-latest?page=with%3Ablock-6acd09138f084a13d13c9fbd#block-6acd09138f084a13d13c9fbd">one question about this</a>, Burnham told a Tory MP he was “getting way ahead of himself” with the question. But one well-placed observer is not being so coy.</p><p><strong>Neil Kinnock</strong>, the former Labour leader and one of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/jul/17/andy-burnham-labour-leader-speech-latest-news-updates?page=with%3Ablock-6a5a15d78f085bcdc0081c3b#block-6a5a15d78f085bcdc0081c3b">three people Burnham has named as his political mentors</a>, has given <a href="https://www.repubblica.it/esteri/2026/10/13/news/interview_with_lord_kinnock_andy_burnham_s_objective_is_to_join_the_eu_again-425643584/">an interview</a> to la Repubblica, the Italian newspaper. He told it that he believes Burnham does want to, and will, take the UK back into the EU.</p><p>Yes, sure, sure, sure. His commitment is authentic. He really does understand from the grassroots up why restoring what I think of as normality in our continent is vital for every party economically, politically, culturally, all in security terms, and is able to articulate it in language that people can understand. So yeah, he is definitely.</p><p>Andy’s not changed direction. He’s always been a committed pro-European. In the byelection, he rightly didn’t make a noise about it. That’s tomorrow’s debate. Simply because the byelection wasn’t about Europe. It was about winning Makerfield in order to enable him to become leader of the party. That’s all it was about.</p><p>It’s common sense. It’s not left and right. Andy’s view of the engagement of the state is about what Winston Churchill did in the 1950s, and I don’t remember Churchill being thought of as on the left. Andy’s a socialist, but he’s a very common-sense socialist. He’s very rational. He’s cool, not just with his dark blue T-shirt, but in his thinking, and he’s advanced a hell of a lot in the last 10–12 years in terms of his understanding of the absolute importance of utility, of usefulness in politics.</p><p>That’s what puts us, basically, he and I, on the same spot. Of course he’s on the left. I’m on the left. We’re socialists, but we are prompted by the usefulness of the application of ideas.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2026/oct/13/andy-burnham-brexit-eu-europe-neil-kinnock-lobby-wes-streeting-labour-prisoner-early-release-uk-politics-latest-news-updates">Continue reading...</a></description>
